part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `ExpressionScopeHandler.parseFunctionBody` (packages/babel-parser/src/util/expression-scope.js:113): when a function/arrow had an **expression** body (e.g. `()=>null` as a parameter default), the pushed `ExpressionScope` was never popped — the pop only ran in the block-body branch. That left the scope stack unbalanced, so a later `exit()` popped the wrong scope, leaving a `ParameterDeclaration` scope active. Consequently `await`/`yield` later in the enclosing function body hit `recordParameterInitializerError` and were wrongly rejected.

The fix moves `this.stack.pop()` after the if/else so it always runs (same as upstream babel/babel#13928). All 10737 babel-parser tests pass; the 4 babel-core test failures are pre-existing on the unmodified tree.
